text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: hosted.gpu.queue_length > 4000 in us-west-1a. Autoscaler failing to reach desired capacity. Severity: P1. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosts/gpu-queues

Dave-oncall: I'm on it — checking graphs now. queue spike started ~10:00 UTC. Autoscaler desired=120 actual=80, recent node flaps visible.

Carol-runtime: tailing runtime logs on affected nodes (gpu-us-west-1a-*) — seeing repeated Xid/OOM. Looks like driver oom kills. Pasting snippet: 
```
Mar 15 10:03:22 gpu-node-12 kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=12345, Process name: python3
Mar 15 10:03:22 gpu-node-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (python3) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

Bob-sre: autoscaler logs show repeated scale ups but many nodes fail registration during provisioning -> autoscaler backs off. Also seeing repeated container restarts for runtime-driver on the nodes that do come up. Suggest we disable autoscaler to stop thrash.

Dave-oncall: Customer impact check: hosted generation latency > 8s for many routes, 5xx rate ~35% in 10:00-10:20 window. Emily, ping support + top customers?

Emily-support: Notifying top customers now: NovaChat, Voxly, Transcribe.ai. Messaging NovaChat: "We're investigating GPU instability; temporarily switching to smaller model to reduce timeouts. ETA 30-45m." They acknowledged.

Carol-runtime: runtime agent reports KV cache corruption after OOM on several pods; restart required to recover. I'm going to restart runtime driver on the three worst nodes.

Sean-ops: Running cordon/drain for noisy nodes now: 
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

Alice-enginfra: I can bring up a reserved spare pool in us-east-1 (+20 GPUs) to absorb traffic. Starting provisioning of reserved instances now.

Dave-oncall: Good. While spare capacity comes up, let's throttle incoming traffic and enable smaller-model fallbacks for non-enterprise routes. Mark, can product flip the routing?

Mark-product: Enabling fallback to redwood-medium for non-enterprise routes and reducing route concurrency for /v1/generate. Applying change now.

Dave-oncall: Also lowering per-route max concurrent to 4 to slow queue growth: 
`redwoodctl apply --set route./v1/generate.concurrency=4`

Carol-runtime: After the three driver restarts Xid errors stopped on those nodes. New nodes still show memory leak patterns. Suspect recent NVIDIA driver 530.41 rollout.

Bob-sre: We should rollback driver on canary nodes. If 530.41 correlates with failure windows, rollback to 530.36. Also disable autoscaler for now to avoid repeated provisioning/teardown cycles.

Alice-enginfra: Starting rollback canary to 530.36 on two nodes in us-west-1a. Will monitor for 10m before wider roll.

Sean-ops: Queue length trending down from 4200 -> 800 after throttles and fallbacks. :white_check_mark:

Carol-runtime: One node still flapping with OOM even after driver restart. Capturing dmesg and nv-hostengine logs and escalating to hardware diagnostics.

Bob-sre: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Disable autoscaler (prevent thrash), 2) cordon/drain/restart drivers on nodes with Xid, 3) rollback driver on canary, 4) bring spare reserved capacity, 5) enable model fallbacks and rate-limits, 6) notify customers + status page. Postmortem actions: detect 'driver OOM Xid' to pause autoscale, bump min spare per region, add canary driver rollouts.

Emily-support: Status page update drafted and sent to status.redwood.ai. Customers notified: NovaChat switched to medium model, Voxly in progress.

Incident-bot: Incident ticket created INC-2026-1872. Ops channel updated.

Dave-oncall: Handoff plan: I'll stay until 11:00 UTC, then hand to bob-sre for RCA. Current time 10:25 UTC. Please add notes to the incident doc.

Bob-sre: Taking lead at 11:00. I'll coordinate root cause and remediation. Starting collection of full node logs and autoscaler history.

Mark-product: Tracking cost & impact for the burst to reserved pool; will update finance with estimate.

Emily-support: I will follow up with customers in 30m with ETA and mitigation summary.

Carol-runtime: After rollback canary started, no new Xid on canary nodes for 12m. If stable, we'll roll 530.36 wider.

Sean-ops: Re-enable autoscaler only after driver rollback completes and cooldown increased. Suggest new cooldown=15m and increase max node registration timeout.

Bob-sre: Agreed. Add automation: if node Xid rate > 3 per 10m, autoscaler should pause and mark nodes for maint.

Dave-oncall: Summary: root-cause likely driver regression (530.41) causing OOMs/Xid, which reduced effective GPU capacity and tripped autoscaler into oscillation. Mitigations: driver rollback, cordon/drain noisy nodes, reserved pool bump, throttles/fallbacks, autoscaler disable and config changes. Owners assigned. Will write short incident summary and link to postmortem template.

Bob-sre: I'll lead postmortem and own follow-ups. Assign action items: carol-runtime (driver logs + reproduce), alice-enginfra (rollback & canary), sean-ops (autoscaler rules), emily-support (customer comms), mark-product (cost report).

Dave-oncall: Thanks all. I'll close this active thread and move the incident doc to postmortems after RCA. :thumbsup:
